Jazz Oral History Project
Interview with Jimmy Maxwell
Reel 3
Conducted by Milt Hinton

PRO-TYPISTS, INC.
PROFESSIONAL TRANSCRIPTION SERVICE
AREA CODE 202 347-5395
This is Wednesday, May 2nd, 1979, and Jimmy Maxwell, here you are, you and I, Milt Hinton, in New Orleans, Louisiana, at the Jazz Festival.
No, this is the New Orleans Jazz Festival, but George Wein brings a lot of people and I don't know if he handles the whole festival. I don't think so.

But this is marvelous, you're down here, I saw so many wonderful people last night. We opened here last night in the Hyatt House, and you guys came by and Jimmy played for us, and Eubie Blake and who else, Illionois Jacquet, Lionel Hampton. It was quite some opening night, Eddie B&G. George Wein even played. So we thought we'd take this opportunity, Jimmy, just you and I to continue our history, which we started in New York City, this is the last portion of it. And I'd like to get into some of the things you were talking about. We were talking about your life, the commercial end, but what about some of the commercial end, you've been playing in the studios and recording. What's your impression of it and how do you think it can be improved?
